line: You've named your own method: "something I call 'Leadership Architecture'."
notes: Switched to rank 2 after the coordinator flagged two problems with the rank 1 pick: the earlier clause ('your weekly coffee ritual') misdescribed a post actually about a 5:30am boot camp, and the earlier quote ('how I met Paraic initially.') named a stranger the reader can't place without reconstructing context.

Rank 2's quote is his own coined term for his own method, legible on its own with no outside reference needed, dated 11 days ago, and unrepeatable by anyone else — same category as another lead's self-named diagnostic that verified cleanly.

Rejected rank 1 outright rather than fixing the clause: the boot camp/community material didn't have a shorter self-contained span that both named something distinctive and stood alone without more surrounding sentence than the hook room allows.
Rejected rank 3 (About page) as undated, third-person career summary with no recency signal.
Quote and clause fit the 20-word hook_room for this lead (anchors.json).

Shipped email quotes the contiguous sub-span ‘Leadership Architecture’ from within the certified quote, not the full fragment. The certified fragment carries his first-person ‘something I call’, and on a cold read that ‘I’ resolves to the sender, since every other ‘I’ in the email is Haytham. Three drafts failed on that collision (unmarked, then ‘You wrote’, then ‘You gave the work your own name’); signposting it did not clear it. The sub-span is verbatim and re-fetchable against the same observation and post, and attribution is carried by the sentence around it (‘is your own name for the work’). hook_quote left as certified; this note exists so the CRM record and the shipped email do not disagree silently.
